title: Structured-output sampling: constrained laws, acceptance and repair under an allowed set
description: token-constraints' laws (mask first, then filter) with Core's draws from token-sampling: the law of a row under a matcher's allowed set, a sampled draft accepted with min(1, p/q) and repaired from max(p - q, 0) inside the language. Equals token-sampling on rows masked to the allowed set. Its device form masks each constrained row's logits to its allowed set before token-sampling's device law (sample), or in buffers at fixed addresses filled from the host's bitmask words before the launch, for a step captured in a CUDA graph (staged); inside captured decode rounds (rounds:sampler) token-sampling's round form with each slot's mask staged beside its rules, a constrained slot's logits masked and its drafts cut (one token a round). Core decodes constrained requests one token per step, so sampled verification under a constraint stays the host form.

rounds.description: what samples inside captured decode rounds (rounds:sampler): token-sampling's native round form (its code/sampling.cu built for the device at load; where it does not build, the torch law, with a warning) or its torch law
